established_findings.text: The outage began at 02:14 local time on 14 March when Building 2 lost utility power.
The total duration of the outage was 4 hours and 20 minutes.
A total of 312 customers were affected by the outage.
Building 2, which houses four data halls with roughly 1,900 racks, opened in 2017.
Building 1 on the same campus was not affected by the incident.
The campus is staffed 24/7 by a rotating team of operations engineers.
The UPS system is rated for 15 minutes at full load and the battery strings were installed in 2019.
Both generators are rated at 2 MW each.
The utility provider was notified at 03:05.
The regional weather station recorded clear skies, no precipitation, and no wind above 12 km/h on the night of 13 to 14 March.

unresolved_conflicts.what_would_resolve_it: Clarify the actual UPS runtime from system logs.

unresolved_conflicts.what_would_resolve_it: Verify the fuel level reading at the start of the incident.

unresolved_conflicts.summary: Weather vs cause discrepancy: clear skies vs storm trigger.
unresolved_conflicts.what_would_resolve_it: Determine the actual weather conditions affecting the substation.

unresolved_conflicts.summary: Service restoration vs feed restoration discrepancy: 06:34 vs 08:05.
unresolved_conflicts.what_would_resolve_it: Clarify the timeline of service restoration relative to feed restoration.

conclusion: The outage at Building 2 began at 02:14 on 14 March and lasted 4 hours 20 minutes, affecting 312 customers. Building 2, opened in 2017, houses four data halls with roughly 1,900 racks, while Building 1 remained unaffected. Several key facts remain unresolved, including the exact UPS runtime, failover approval, generator fuel capacity, weather conditions, premium-tier customer count, and the sequence of service restoration. Further investigation is required to resolve these contradictions and determine the root cause.
